contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #353: Affine Bernstein rigidity through dimension nine and a smooth dimension-ten counterexample.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 353 (Affine Bernstein rigidity through dimension nine and a smooth dimension-ten counterexample.; papers: A Smooth Nonquadratic Entire Affine Maximal Graph in Dimension Ten; The affine Bernstein theorem in dimensions three through nine; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/353.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

For a Euclidean-complete smooth strictly convex classical affine maximal graph in dimension 3 <= n <= 9, the largest direction number among the models of geometry.tex Definition def:model in F(D) is one (bounds.tex, prop:one-direction).

Compact tangent caps, affine-limit closure, and maximal-direction centering yield normalized fiber, cap, and interior-ball bounds uniformly over logarithmic positions; only the smooth-approximant threshold may depend on the position.
Every smooth affine image of the graph is affine-area stationary and satisfies area.tex eq:cap-identity with an inward conormal and compactly supported surface tests.
For 3 <= n <= 9 and 2 <= k <= n, smooth stationary convex tubes satisfy tubes.tex prop:log-inequality with a dimension-only constant and compactly supported cutoffs.
A full-dimensional compact cap of an affine limit forces positive affine area on late smooth approximants and nonvanishing logarithmic mass away from all coordinate faces.
Uniform normalized support, compact-cap and interior-ball bounds imply a position-independent bound for sigma on each logarithmic cell of the smooth approximants.
A positive initial mass, a uniform shell-growth inequality, and uniform cell bounds contradict each other on one finite logarithmic box of one sufficiently late smooth approximant.
The origin-preserving linear normalization used in geometry.tex follows from John normalization for nonsymmetric convex bodies.
Rigidity manuscript thm:main: every Euclidean-complete smooth strictly convex classical affine maximal graph in dimensions three through nine is an elliptic paraboloid.
Uniformly balanced tangent sections imply a scale-independent strict-convexity modulus and the cited interior-estimate rescaling argument makes all third derivatives vanish; outside this mission.
Dimension-ten manuscript thm:main: there exists a smooth nonquadratic entire classical affine maximal graph with pointwise positive-definite Hessian on R^10; outside this mission.
Dimension-ten manuscript prop:reduction: positive F,P with D^2F > 0 satisfying det D^2F = F P^(-12/11) and tr((D^2F)^(-1)D^2P)+11P/F=0 give u=sqrt(F^2+t^2) solving the ten-dimensional equation.
Dimension-ten manuscript lem:local: the radial system has a smooth germ through the origin with F(0)=P(0)=1 and Hessians I and -(11/9)I.
Dimension-ten manuscript lem:autonomous and lem:box: logarithmic ratios A,B,D satisfy the displayed autonomous system and remain in [0,9/2] x [0,7/2] x [0,33/7].
Dimension-ten manuscript prop:global: bounds for logarithmic ratios prevent finite-radius breakdown and preserve positive F,P,y,y-prime.
The origin-preserving linear normalization used in geometry.tex follows from John normalization for nonsymmetric convex bodies.

claims.natural_statement: For all positive real determinant data and n>0 the inverse-Hessian weighted interpolation identity holds; for every real 3<=n<=9 the lambda=15/16 quadratic form has uniform coercivity 1/256 in arbitrary finite orthonormal frames; the cap-testing vectors have Gram matrix I+(k+2)11^T; and a finite family of mass-growth inequalities contradicts a smaller finite-box upper bound. This claim formalizes these interfaces only, not the analytic geometry of C_ONE_DIRECTION.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

noncomputable section

namespace CapGrowthAudit

def delta (n : Real) : Real := 1 / (n + 2)

def theta (n : Real) : Real := (n + 2) / (2 * (n + 1))

theorem interpolation_exponents (n : Real) (hn : 0 < n) :
    0 < theta n /\ theta n < 1 /\
      theta n * (1 - delta n) = 1 / 2 /\
      delta n * theta n + (1 - theta n) = 1 / 2 := by
  have h1 : n + 1 > 0 := by linarith
  have h2 : n + 2 > 0 := by linarith
  refine ⟨div_pos h2 (by positivity), ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · unfold theta
    apply (div_lt_one (by positivity : 0 < 2 * (n + 1))).2
    linarith
  · unfold theta delta
    field_simp [ne_of_gt h1, ne_of_gt h2]
    <;> ring
  · unfold theta delta
    field_simp [ne_of_gt h1, ne_of_gt h2]
    <;> ring

theorem weighted_interpolation
    (n D R t : Real) (hn : 0 < n)
    (hD : 0 < D) (hR : 0 < R) (ht : 0 < t) :
    Real.sqrt (D * R) * t =
      (D ^ delta n * R ^ (1 - delta n) * t) ^ theta n *
        (D * t) ^ (1 - theta n) := by
  have h1 : Ne (n + 1) 0 := by linarith
  have h2 : Ne (n + 2) 0 := by linarith
  have hA : 0 < D ^ delta n * R ^ (1 - delta n) * t := by positivity
  have hB : 0 < D * t := mul_pos hD ht
  have hL : 0 < Real.sqrt (D * R) * t := by positivity
  have hU :
      0 < (D ^ delta n * R ^ (1 - delta n) * t) ^ theta n *
        (D * t) ^ (1 - theta n) := by positivity
  have hlog :
      Real.log (Real.sqrt (D * R) * t) =
        Real.log ((D ^ delta n * R ^ (1 - delta n) * t) ^ theta n *
          (D * t) ^ (1 - theta n)) := by
    rw [Real.log_mul (by positivity) (ne_of_gt ht),
      Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.log_rpow (mul_pos hD hR),
      Real.log_mul (ne_of_gt hD) (ne_of_gt hR)]
    rw [Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity),
      Real.log_rpow hA, Real.log_rpow hB]
    rw [Real.log_mul (by positivity) (ne_of_gt ht),
      Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity),
      Real.log_rpow hD, Real.log_rpow hR,
      Real.log_mul (ne_of_gt hD) (ne_of_gt ht)]
    unfold delta theta
    field_simp [h1, h2]
    <;> ring
  calc
    Real.sqrt (D * R) * t =
        Real.exp (Real.log (Real.sqrt (D * R) * t)) := (Real.exp_log hL).symm
    _ = Real.exp (Real.log
        ((D ^ delta n * R ^ (1 - delta n) * t) ^ theta n *
          (D * t) ^ (1 - theta n))) := congrArg Real.exp hlog
    _ = _ := Real.exp_log hU

theorem quadratic_nonnegative
    (a b c p d : Real) (ha : 0 < a) (hdet : 0 <= a * b - c ^ 2) :
    0 <= a * p ^ 2 + 2 * c * p * d + b * d ^ 2 := by
  have hs : 0 <= (a * p + c * d) ^ 2 + (a * b - c ^ 2) * d ^ 2 :=
    add_nonneg (sq_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg hdet (sq_nonneg _))
  have hid :
      (a * p + c * d) ^ 2 + (a * b - c ^ 2) * d ^ 2 =
        a * (a * p ^ 2 + 2 * c * p * d + b * d ^ 2) := by ring
  rw [hid] at hs
  by_contra hneg
  have hneg' : a * p ^ 2 + 2 * c * p * d + b * d ^ 2 < 0 :=
    lt_of_not_ge hneg
  have := mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg ha hneg'
  linarith

theorem scalar_coercivity
    (n p d : Real) (hnlo : 3 <= n) (hnhi : n <= 9) :
    (1 / 256 : Real) * (p ^ 2 + d ^ 2) <=
      (n - 7 / 8) * p ^ 2 + (n + 2) / 2 * p * d + 15 / 16 * d ^ 2 := by
  let a : Real := n - 7 / 8 - 1 / 256
  let b : Real := 15 / 16 - 1 / 256
  let c : Real := (n + 2) / 4
  have ha : 0 < a := by dsimp [a]; linarith
  have hprod : 0 <= (n - 2) * (9 - n) :=
    mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)
  have hdet : 0 <= a * b - c ^ 2 := by
    dsimp [a, b, c]
    nlinarith [hprod]
  have hq := quadratic_nonnegative a b c p d ha hdet
  calc
    (1 / 256 : Real) * (p ^ 2 + d ^ 2) <=
        (1 / 256 : Real) * (p ^ 2 + d ^ 2) +
          (a * p ^ 2 + 2 * c * p * d + b * d ^ 2) :=
      le_add_of_nonneg_right hq
    _ = _ := by dsimp [a, b, c]; ring

theorem finite_coercivity
    (n : Real) (k r : Nat) (hnlo : 3 <= n) (hnhi : n <= 9)
    (hk : 2 <= k) (p d : Fin k -> Real) (z : Fin r -> Real) :
    (1 / 256 : Real) *
        (1 + Finset.univ.sum (fun i => p i ^ 2) +
          Finset.univ.sum (fun i => d i ^ 2) +
          Finset.univ.sum (fun i => z i ^ 2)) <=
      (k : Real) - 15 / 8 +
        Finset.univ.sum (fun i =>
          (n - 7 / 8) * p i ^ 2 + (n + 2) / 2 * p i * d i +
            15 / 16 * d i ^ 2) +
        15 / 16 * Finset.univ.sum (fun i => z i ^ 2) := by
  have hpairs := Finset.sum_le_sum
    (s := Finset.univ) (fun (i : Fin k) _ =>
      scalar_coercivity n (p i) (d i) hnlo hnhi)
  have hkR : (2 : Real) <= k := by exact_mod_cast hk
  have hc : (1 / 256 : Real) <= (k : Real) - 15 / 8 := by linarith
  have hz0 : 0 <= Finset.univ.sum (fun i => z i ^ 2) :=
    Finset.sum_nonneg (fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _)
  have hz :
      (1 / 256 : Real) * Finset.univ.sum (fun i => z i ^ 2) <=
        15 / 16 * Finset.univ.sum (fun i => z i ^ 2) := by linarith
  calc
    _ = (1 / 256 : Real) +
        Finset.univ.sum (fun i => (1 / 256 : Real) * (p i ^ 2 + d i ^ 2)) +
        (1 / 256 : Real) * Finset.univ.sum (fun i => z i ^ 2) := by
      simp only [mul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib, <- Finset.mul_sum]
      ring
    _ <= _ := add_le_add (add_le_add hc hpairs) hz

theorem frame_gram (k : Nat) (i j : Fin k) :
    (Finset.univ.sum (fun r : Fin k =>
      (1 + if r = i then 1 else 0 : Real) *
        (1 + if r = j then 1 else 0 : Real))) =
      (if i = j then 1 else 0 : Real) + (k : Real) + 2 := by
  classical
  have hid (r : Fin k) :
      (1 + if r = i then 1 else 0 : Real) *
          (1 + if r = j then 1 else 0 : Real) =
        1 + (if r = i then 1 else 0 : Real) +
          (if r = j then 1 else 0 : Real) +
          (if r = i then (if i = j then 1 else 0 : Real) else 0) := by
    split_ifs <;> simp_all <;> ring
  simp_rw [hid]
  simp only [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  simp
  <;> ring

theorem recurrence_lower
    (mass : Nat -> Real) (q c : Real) (N : Nat)
    (hq : 0 <= q) (h0 : c <= mass 0)
    (hstep : forall l : Nat, l < N -> q * mass l <= mass (l + 1)) :
    c * q ^ N <= mass N := by
  have h : forall t : Nat, t <= N -> c * q ^ t <= mass t := by
    intro t
    induction t with
    | zero =>
        intro _
        simpa using h0
    | succ t ih =>
        intro ht
        have htN : t < N := by omega
        have hi := ih (by omega)
        calc
          c * q ^ (t + 1) = q * (c * q ^ t) := by rw [pow_succ]; ring
          _ <= q * mass t := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hi hq
          _ <= mass (t + 1) := hstep t htN
  exact h N (Nat.le_refl N)

theorem finite_box_contradiction
    (mass : Nat -> Real) (q c upper : Real) (N : Nat)
    (hq : 0 <= q) (h0 : c <= mass 0)
    (hstep : forall l : Nat, l < N -> q * mass l <= mass (l + 1))
    (hupper : mass N <= upper) (hchoice : upper < c * q ^ N) : False := by
  have hlower := recurrence_lower mass q c N hq h0 hstep
  linarith

end CapGrowthAudit

claims.natural_statement: For every compact full-dimensional convex K in R^d with d>=1 and 0 in K, an origin-preserving linear map gives B_1(c) subset AK subset B_(2d(d+1))(c); maximal-volume simplex normalization proves this without the John theorem. With -K subset C_* K it also gives a centered inner ball of radius 2/(C_*+1).

For every n>=2 and 1<=k<=n, a smooth stationary positively curved convex tube with c_1<=h<=C_1 on [1/4,4]^k, a fixed interior ball centered at (1,0), and uniformly bounded compact caps for the finitely many positive forms 1+e_r has uniformly bounded logarithmic mass sigma on [1/2,2]^k. Section 6 proves this without pointwise inverse-Hessian bounds or regularity of a limiting body.

For every k>=1, l_0>=1, c_0,C_box>0 and q>1, an integer N>=2(k+1), N>=l_0+1 and N>(C_box/c_0) 2^(2k+1)(k+1)!/(q-1)^(k+1) satisfies c_0 q^N>C_box(l_0+N+1)^k. This finite explicit horizon permits choosing a single late approximant afterwards.

For every integer n>=2 and 1<=k<=n, let E be a closed full-dimensional convex body in R^(n+1) whose smooth positively curved boundary is stationary for affine area. Suppose its compact fibers contain zero in their interiors over [1/4,4]^k, with fixed 0<c_1<=h<=C_1, a fixed interior ball centered at (1,0), and, for every r=1,...,k, a compact cap (1+e_r).s<=b_0 contained in a fixed ball, where the common fixed top b_0>2(k+1). Then sigma([1/2,2]^k) has a bound depending only on these fixed data and n,k, without pointwise inverse-Hessian bounds or regularity of a limiting body. Section 6 proves this uniform local cell theorem.
